name: Williamson Hall

renovations.what: Planned renovation with Christensen (interiors, bathrooms, common areas, heating and plumbing); $32.3M deferred maintenance. Status not confirmed.

facts.text: Dedicated June 10, 1972 and named for Dean P. Williamson (class of 1932), alumni trustee and board chair.
Housing lists 424 students (large hall), first-year only, traditional singles and doubles, meal plan required; floor 2B is a gender-inclusive community.
Each floor is made of one to three towers (wings); a lobby duty desk lends games and cooking supplies 8-10 pm, and the main lounge has a fireplace.
Features: elevator, kitchen, laundry, indoor bike storage, sports courts; floor plans list ten floors; strobe/speaker alerts in all rooms. No AC listed.

UNH Facilities lists a Williamson & Christensen renovation: at 50 years old the interiors are worn, bathrooms and common spaces need modernizing, and heating and plumbing systems are failing; the project addresses $32.3 million in deferred maintenance.

verdict: Christensen's stepped brick twin: a sculptural Late Modern tower outside, worn rooms and no A/C inside, renovation pending.
notes: Commons photo (2013): sculpted ten-storey tower of smooth red brick, stepped setbacks and slot/bay windows; strong, monolithic massing, a distinctive Late Modern composition. Reference room photo: tall window, scuffed vinyl floor, plain white walls, average ceiling; dated finishes. Archives do not name Williamson's architect; Franzen is likely (twin of Christensen) but unconfirmed, so architect left null. The old row's 1969-70 dates are unsourced; only the 1972 dedication is documented. $70M/$76M cost figures seen only in search snippets (not opened). Alias "Willy" from Housing image filenames only; treat as informal.
judgeNotes: Photos show strong massing. Matches Christensen. The planned 2026 renovation is marked major: false until it is done.
